label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

This looks like a CRLF line-ending issue, consistent with the new Windows export tool. `parseStatement` splits the input on `"\n"` only (`text.split("\n")`), so on Windows-style CRLF files each line keeps a trailing `\r`. For the header row, that means the last column name becomes `"description\r"` instead of `"description"`, which fails the `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some(column => !header.includes(column))` check in `assertShape` for the header itself (index 0 → reported as "row 1"), even though the column count matches and the file looks fine in a spreadsheet.

Fix would be to split on `/\r?\n/` (or strip a trailing `\r` from each line) before parsing the header and rows in `parser.ts`.

input.title: Handle CRLF line endings in CSV parser
input.body: File: src/ingest/parser.ts. The parser splits input only on "\n", so files with Windows-style CRLF line endings (as now produced by finance's new export tool) leave a trailing "\r" on the last field of each line, including the header. This makes the last header column (e.g. "description\r") fail to match REQUIRED_COLUMNS, triggering the "Malformed row" error on row 1 even though the columns are correct. Fix by splitting on /\r?\n/ (or stripping a trailing "\r" from each line) before parsing the header and rows.
